newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Easing milling wheat in focus on Hungary BCE.
newsitem.headline: Easing milling wheat in focus on Hungary BCE.

text.p: Limit falls in some milling wheat futures featured in Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) trading on Monday, with further falls possible, dealers said.
"It is possible that milling wheat prices could drop further," said Dezso Kormendi of LaSalle Tozsdeugynoki Rt.
Milling wheat futures dropped the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for maturities from December onward while August eased 120 forints, September dropped 390 and October 350 forints.
The nearby contract was the only one to buck the trend, rising 150 forints to 20,750 but Kormendi said that was not surprising given that it was close to its delivery time.
"This is a recurring phenomenon as delivery approaches," he said.
July maize also rose 200 forints to 21,000 due to position-closing while other maize contracts finished slightly lower, dropping 70 to 190 forints for the October to March positions.
The two most distant, May and July 1998, were flat and tradeless.
Total grains turnover on the BCE was a modest 1,496 lots or 648.93 million forints, up from Friday's 1,183 lots or 503.68 million forints.
Milling wheat futures accounted for the bulk of the turnover in volume terms with 1,081 lots.
